checks: All positive sources of a representation at z lie in its minimal face by its supporting equalities. If z is not a vertex, the other sites include every vertex of that face and their hull is the face. Assign each other site a small positive weight, subtract, and normalize: the residual stays in a relative-interior neighborhood and has a convex representation there. This constructs a single hyperedge containing the entire face trace, including z as anchor.

For any site in conv(A), a nontrivial representation uses only sources from its component. A trivial representation has the site already in A. The reverse inclusion uses monotonicity of convex hulls. Taking A to be a component shows it is closed, hence lattice-complete if P is.

For Helly upper additivity choose a certificate on each component and take their union. For the reverse, the finite definition supplies a minimal empty family of size h(P_i) on each component (including h=1). Each trace extends by the other components to a closed trace by the split formula. All extended traces have empty intersection, and deleting any one retains that trace’s own component witness. The deletion witnesses also rule out duplicate extended traces.

Distinct components cannot meet the same occupied parity class: the midpoint of such a pair is a site by completeness and its nontrivial representation connects the endpoints. This proves exact additivity of the occupied counts in the common affine lattice.

The ambient cap uses one mark 0 in R per site. Complete P supplies every same-parity graph midpoint, and C×R has exactly the trace of C on the zero graph. The accepted graph theorem thus gives h(P)≤2^n. The exact Helly split converts this into the claimed cap on the sum.
